What Is a Spinal Cord Injury?

A spinal cord injury can describe any damage to the spinal cord, including the vertebrae, disks, nerves, and surrounding fluids and tissues. A spinal cord injury can stem from a blow to the back, the spine bending in the wrong direction, or the spine being crushed or severed. There are different types of spinal cord injuries depending on where the injury falls on the back:
Cervical spinal cord injury. The uppermost portion of the back, including vertebrae in the neck.
Thoracic spinal cord injury. The part of the spinal cord in the middle of the back.
Lumbar spinal cord injury. The lower-middle portion of the spine.
Sacrum or coccyx injury. The five bottommost vertebrae and the tailbone.

These injuries can cause catastrophic damage to a victim, including permanent paralysis. In general, the higher up on the spinal cord the injury, the more severe the symptoms. A cervical spinal cord injury can result in quadriplegia, for example, or paralysis from the neck down. All spinal cord injuries are serious and require emergency medical care.
Do You Have a Case?

You may have grounds to file a spinal cord injury lawsuit in Thornton, Colorado if one or more parties had the power to prevent your injury but negligently failed to do so. In personal injury law, negligence is the failure of an individual or entity to exercise reasonable care, resulting in harm or injury to another person.

In general, you or your attorney will need to prove – based on clear and convincing evidence – that the defendant owed you a duty of care, negligently breached this duty, and caused your accident. There must be proof that the defendant committed an act or omission that a reasonable and prudent person would not have in the same circumstances and that this caused your injury.
